programme.title: Brainstorm: Unraveling The Mysteries Of The Brain
programme.desc: Small-town neuroscientists revolutionize our understanding of the brain.

programme.title: Groundwork: Building Community Through Regenerative Rubber
programme.desc: Thailand is the world’s largest exporter of rubber, and Chorthip is a key - farmer demonstrating and leading a shift to regenerative agroforestry methods. She’s transformed her land from a rubber monoculture to a diverse rubber forest garden, implementing organic practices that improve the quality of life for both her family and her - community.

programme.title: Horndribbles
programme.desc: Step into the handmade world of Horndribbles, a - documentary where puppeteer Lucas Richards builds - more than characters—he builds connection, - community, and meaning through the art of puppetry. Directed by Savannah Warrick.

programme.title: Groundwork: A Family Journey Into Regenerative Cotton
programme.desc: When a family cotton farm defies the conventions holding them back—they embark on a journey of transformation that radically shifts their farm, their family, and their future. Directed by Lindsey Hagen.

programme.title: Quiet Minds Silent Streets
programme.desc: Quiet Minds Silent Streets introduces viewers to a community that has been chronically affected by gun violence. This thoughtful, eye-opening documentary asks whether they can find a new way forward with a relatively simple technique: mindfulness and meditation. Executive produced by Director X and directed by Karen Chapman.

programme.title: The Thousand Year Journey
programme.desc: "Routine is the enemy of time." Jedidiah Jenkins rides his bicycle from Oregon to Patagonia, the southern tip of South America, while expounding upon ideas that made him leave a job he loved for the open road. Directed by Kenny Laubbacher.

programme.title: Second Winds
programme.desc: A film that reveals how a life-changing diagnosis can bring renewed clarity and purpose.

programme.title: The Magic Of Chess
programme.desc: Filmed at the 2019 Elementary Chess Championships at the Nashville Opryland resort, a group of children share their insights about the benefits of chess. Directed by Jenny Schweitzer Bell.

programme.title: Haiti On Fire
programme.desc: Haiti on Fire chronicles Haiti’s descent into violence and chaos, documenting the rise of Barbecue and the G9 gang alliance.

programme.title: The Undocumented Lawyer
programme.desc: Lizbeth Mateo is an attorney who swore to uphold the Constitution. She’s also undocumented. When a client takes sanctuary in a church, Lizbeth’s own experience guides their fight for justice. Directed by Chris Temple and Zach Ingrasci.

programme.title: Paperboy Love Prince Runs for Mayor
programme.desc: Rapper and street performer Paperboy Love Prince takes on the political elite in the race for NYC mayor. Directed by Owen Dubeck.

programme.title: Hands Up, Chin Down - Censored
programme.desc: Hands Up, Chin Down is a short documentary about Jerry Mitchell, one of the most respected coaches in amateur boxing. Based on a series of raw audio recordings and lasting exactly the length of a round of boxing, the film is a conceptual study of the coaching process with its strange mix of brutality and care. World premiere at Sheffield Doc/Fest 2018.

programme.title: Betty Feeds The Animals
programme.desc: Betty loves animals, she loves them so much that everyday she puts 30 bowls of food outside of her home to feed them. She feeds skunks, raccoons, cats, foxes and the occasional opossum. This is her story. Directed by James P. Gannon.

programme.desc: A group of friends race to find a legendary creature in Minnesota’s waters.

programme.title: Isolated
programme.desc: Five world class surfers travel to New Guinea in search of undiscovered waves, but end up discovering so much more.

programme.title: And Two If By Sea
programme.desc: The story of iconic professional surfers and identical twins CJ & Damien Hobgood. Their sibling rivalry and struggle to each establish their own identity fueled their careers, but ripped their personal and peripheral relationships apart.

programme.title: Understory
programme.desc: Three women set sail on a 350 mile expedition through Alaska’s massive Tongass National Forest, exploring how clearcut logging in this coastal rainforest could affect wildlife, local communities and our planet’s climate.

programme.title: Caffeinated
programme.desc: Learn the story behind your morning Joe. From seed to mug, coffee, and the process by which it is created, has shaped the lives of thousands of individuals worldwide. Caffeinated gives the coffee consumer unprecedented access to the farmers responsible for growing that perfect bean, and the roasters and baristas responsible for brewing that perfect cup. Directed by Vishal Solanki.

programme.title: After Antarctica
programme.desc: After Antarctica follows legendary polar explorer Will Steger’s journey as an eyewitness to the greatest changes to the polar regions of our planet. Now, thirty years after his historic expedition across the coldest continent on Earth, Steger heads out on the ice once again, at a time when he is not only known for being the first in history to complete these historic feats - he is also the last. Directed by Tasha Van Zandt.

programme.title: Deep Web
programme.desc: The deep web caught the attention of the world with the arrest of Ross William Ulbricht - the convicted entrepreneur accused of being 'Dread Pirate Roberts'. This documentary seeks to unravel the web of secrecy, accusation, and criminal activity surrounding Ulbricht, and also explores how the outcome his trial set a precedent for the future of technological freedom. Directed by Alex Winter.

programme.title: Knuckleball
programme.desc: A documentary that showcases baseball's most unpredictable pitch - follow the journey of the last professional knuckleball pitchers. Tim Wakefield, a 17-year Red Sox veteran, and Mets up-and-comer R.A. Dickey, with just four other living knuckleballers, shine a light on their remarkable brotherhood and the shared pursuit of honor and craftsmanship. Directed by Annie Sundberg.

programme.title: Once Upon a Time in Uganda
programme.desc: Set in the heart of Uganda, two unlikely friends from opposite sides of the world unite over their shared love of Chuck Norris and gonzo 80’s action flicks. With sheer determination and an outrageous sense of humor, they team up to create their own explosive movies, catapulting Wakaliwood to international stardom and bringing laughter and joy to millions. Directed by Cathryne Czubek.

programme.title: We Could Be King
programme.desc: True story of two rival high school football teams forced to merge into one and their struggle to become champions against all odds. An unflinching snapshot of the power of sports to bring young people, neighborhoods, and a city together. Directed by Judd Ehrlich.

programme.title: A View From The Window
programme.desc: An immersive glimpse of a school day through the eyes of deaf children. Follow a third grade class at the California School for the Deaf in Fremont as they learn about everything from marine life to police harassment. Directed by Christian Filippone and Azar Kafaei.

programme.title: Cherry Pop: The Story Of The World's Fanciest Cat
programme.desc: Cherry Pop was no ordinary cat. Beloved by her wealthy socialite owners, she lived life in the lap of luxury. This delightful story will tickle your funny bone and touch your heart. Directed by Kareem Tabsch.

programme.title: Dolphin Lover
programme.desc: Dolphin Lover is a critically acclaimed, award winning short documentary on the incredible true story of Malcolm Brenner and his summer long love affair with Dolly the dolphin. Directed by Joey Daoud and Kareem Tabsch.

programme.title: Down Again - Censored
programme.desc: DOWN AGAIN is an examination of the connection between mental illness and creativity told through the lens of photographer and Chimaira frontman Mark Hunter, exploring the catharsis of making music and how the art affects the fans.

programme.title: Eleanor Ambos Interiors
programme.desc: As a celebrated interior designer loses her eyesight to macular degeneration, she begins to see her life's work in a new light. This eccentric renegade topples ageist stereotypes as she grapples with the limitations of her aging body. Directed by Katrina Sorrentino and Andrew Ellis.

programme.title: Gotta Groove Records
programme.desc: A short film on the history and resurgence of vinyl records from the perspective of an artist focused pressing plant in Cleveland, Ohio. A hero story about grit, manufacturing and warm tones. Directed by Nick Cavalier.

programme.title: How To Make A Rainbow
programme.desc: The story of a young girl and her mother, observed over the course of two years, as they move together through transitions of home, identity and name. Directed by Ryan Maxey.

programme.title: Jonah
programme.desc: An interview with a formerly enslaved African American man accompanies a powerful modern day dance vignette. The juxtaposition of past and present raises questions about inherited trauma and the possibility of regeneration. Directed by Andrew Michael Ellis.

programme.title: Muxes
programme.desc: In the southern state of Oaxaca where, in the indigenous communities around the town of Juchitán, the world is not divided simply into males and females. The local Zapotec people have made room for a third category, which they call “muxes” - men who consider themselves women and live in a socially sanctioned limbo between the two genders. Directed by Ivan Olita.
